name: code_search
description:
Search Ledgerline's codebase for a literal piece of text, case-insensitively, line by line. It matches the contents of lines, never file names, and never the config/ directory. Use it to find which files contain an error message, an identifier or a word from the issue, then read the most likely file with code_read_file. It costs one local read and no money; each call costs a turn, so search for one distinctive term at a time rather than a sentence.

Returns JSON: {"query": <your query, echoed>, "path_glob": <your filter, echoed>, "query_valid": true, "count": <every matching line>, "shown": <lines in results>, "truncated": <true when count > shown>, "source": "index" or "live_files", "index_age": <how old the index is, e.g. "22 days ago">, "results": [{"path": "src/api/uploads.ts", "line": 42, "text": ...}]}, in path order. A response is capped: concise shows at most 10 matching lines, each cut to 120 characters; detailed shows at most 20, each cut to 300 characters. When "truncated" is true, narrow the query or set path_glob rather than asking again.

No match is a success: "count": 0, "results": [], "query_valid": true means the text appears nowhere in the searched files; try a different term. A malformed search is an error, never an empty result: a query that is empty or only whitespace, a query longer than 200 characters, or a path_glob that is not a valid glob.

query.description: The literal text to find, 1 to 200 characters, matched case-insensitively as a substring of one line. No operators: AND, OR, quotes, wildcards and regular expressions are searched for as literal characters. A short distinctive term (an identifier such as withRetry, or a phrase from an error message) finds the responsible line; a long sentence usually finds nothing.

path_glob.description: null searches every file. A glob relative to the repository root, such as "src/**/*.ts" or "src/{api,db}/*.ts", restricts the search to matching files: choose it when a query matches too many lines ("truncated": true) or the issue names an area of the code. It uses letters, digits, / . _ - and the wildcards * ? [ ] { }; it cannot start with / or contain ..

source.description: index, the normal choice, searches the prebuilt index, which is fast but as old as its index_age. live_files reads every file from disk instead: slower, and needed only when the code may have changed since the index was built, or when an index search found nothing that the issue says must exist.

response_format.description: concise, the cheap default, returns at most 10 matching lines of 120 characters: enough to choose a file. detailed returns at most 20 lines of 300 characters and costs about four times the tokens; choose it only when concise lines were cut before the part you need.

examples.note: The typical call: one identifier, the whole codebase, the index, concise.

A hard case: a phrase from an error message that matched too many lines, narrowed to one directory with a glob (not a filter expression such as dir:src/api), with detailed lines because the concise ones were cut.
